name: Cold Call — Outbound Dialer / Batch Runner (D)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ phoneNumberId: $env.VAPI_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, assistantId: $env.VAPI_ASSISTANT_ID, customer: { number: $json.phone }, assistantOverrides: { variableValues: { firma: $json.firma, branche: $json.branche, kontakt_nachname: $json.kontakt_nachname, disclosure_line: $json.disclosure_line } }, metadata: { lead_id: $json.lead_id, session_id: $json.session_id } }) }}

_import_notes: Validated via n8n-mcp validate_workflow (valid:true, 0 errors). BEFORE going live (do WITH user): (1) create n8n HTTP Header Auth credential 'Vapi Bearer' = Authorization: Bearer <VAPI_API_KEY>, attach to 'Vapi: place call'; (2) attach Notion credential to both Notion nodes; (3) set n8n env VAPI_PHONE_NUMBER_ID + VAPI_ASSISTANT_ID; (4) add Lead-DB fields 'Stern Opt-Out'(checkbox) + 'Call Attempts'(number) + 'AI Cold Call' option on 'Outreach Channel'; (5) VERIFY the ICP list + property names ('phone','Firma','Branche','Pipeline Stage','Last contacted') against the live Lead-DB schema, and confirm the Notion update propertyValues key/value format on a sandbox page; (6) keep INACTIVE; first live dial is HALT-gated (notify-telegram halt + poll), Phase 1 max_calls=1 to a founder phone. Default dry_run=true returns the eligible list without dialing. responseMode=lastNode makes the webhook wait for the batch — fine for dry-run + small batches; for large live batches switch to async. Open the app session (POST /api/voice/session/start) or have the app upsert on first /call.
